name: app
//: Point the platform at ANY application by editing .env — URLs and credentials never live here. The one exception is "application": it names the config/apps/<application>/ directory this run uses, so it is pinned here rather than read from .env. An ambient variable choosing which module map (and which entry-state proofs) apply is SEC-2's shape: the thing that decides where a run goes must not come from the source that can redirect it.
//users: The primary user is REQUIRED and has no default, so an unset variable refuses by name. It was an EMPTY default, which resolved to a blank the schema accepts — an unconfigured run then reached a login attempt and failed as though the password were wrong. A second role is OPTIONAL and is therefore ABSENT rather than blank: add a "user" entry here naming APP_USER2_USERNAME and APP_USER2_PASSWORD when you have one. Nothing reads it today (measured 2026-10-01: only users.admin is read anywhere), and a test that asks for a role this file does not define is refused by name via requireUser(). NOTE: this comment must not spell a placeholder in ${...} form — interpolate() walks every string value in this file, including this one, and would try to resolve it.
